facts: Las Vegas was founded as a city in 1905 after land was auctioned off by the San Pedro railroad.
The famous Las Vegas Strip is actually located in the unincorporated town of Paradise, Nevada.
Las Vegas translates to "The Meadows" in Spanish, named for its natural wild grasses and spring waters.
The iconic "Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas" sign was designed by Betty Willis in 1959.
Vegas boasts some of the brightest lights on Earth, visible even from outer space.
High-stakes marathon runners often compete in the annual Rock 'n' Roll Las Vegas Marathon at night.
Temperatures in the surrounding Mojave Desert regularly exceed one hundred degrees Fahrenheit during summer months.
The city hosts world-class entertainment, earning its reputation as the Entertainment Capital of the World.
Nearby Red Rock Canyon offers spectacular sandstone formations and challenging trail runs for outdoor enthusiasts.
The famous Fountains of Bellagio choreograph water shows synchronized to music and light along the Boulevard.
Las Vegas became a boxing capital by hosting legendary bouts featuring champions like Muhammad Ali and Mike Tyson.
The Hoover Dam, located just southeast of the city, was completed during the Great Depression.
The city features luxury restaurants led by famous celebrity chefs from around the world.
Nevada is the largest producer of gold in the United States, deeply tied to the region's mining history.
The Stratosphere Tower stands as the tallest freestanding observation tower in the United States.
Las Vegas is home to the NFL's Las Vegas Raiders and the NHL's Vegas Golden Knights.
The Sphinx replica outside the Luxor Hotel stands taller than the original Great Sphinx of Giza.
Tennis legend Andre Agassi was born and raised right here in Las Vegas.
Lake Mead, created by the Hoover Dam, provides water to millions of people across Nevada and Arizona.
Neon lights have defined the city's nightlife architecture since the first neon sign was installed in 1928.
